questions.knowledge_point: Solve a Variable in a Vector Lying in the Null Space of a Given Matrix
questions.problem: Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}k \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $k$ such that $b\in \text{Null}(A).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $b\in \text{Null}(A),$ then we must have $Ab=0.$ Substituting the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ab & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}k \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}k+9 \\ 2k+18\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}k+9=0 \\ 2k+18=0\end{aligned}
$$

and for each of these equations, we obtain $k=-9.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Null Space of a Given Matrix
questions.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

The second equation tells us that ${x}_{2}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{1}+2(0)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=0.
$$

So, we conclude that $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ is the only solution to this system.

Therefore, $\text{Null}(A)={0}.$
